texts.li: [funeral,lowtech] {DEAD}, headman of {PLACE} for thirty years, has died. {DEAD} kept the town fed through many hard winters, and {FACTION} want to bury their headman in the old way: a deep grave with a stone over it, and a meal for every mourner who comes in from the hills.\n\nThe town can't make everything in time for the burial, and their rider has brought the colony a list of what they still need.

[funeral,!lowtech] {DEAD}, mayor of {PLACE} for thirty years, has died at a great age. {FACTION} want every mourner fed and a proper grave for the one who kept the town going through the bad winters, but the town is short of what it needs.\n\nA courier has brought the colony a list of what is missing, and the date it is needed by.

[wedding,lowtech] {DEAD}, the only daughter of {PLACE}'s headman, is getting married, and {FACTION} want a big wedding: food for every guest, drink for the dancing, and something fine for the couple's new house.\n\nThey can't make it all in time. The headman's rider brought the colony a list, with a message: "We have the will, but not the hands."

[wedding,!lowtech] {DEAD}, only daughter of the mayor of {PLACE}, is getting married, and the mayor has promised the whole region a wedding to remember. {FACTION}'s own kitchens have already said it can't be done in time.\n\nA courier brought the colony the shortfall, item by item, with a delivery date and a polite request not to mention it to the bride.

[funeral,royalhost] {DEAD} of {FACTION} has died at {PLACE}, and the Empire buries its nobility with ceremony: every mourner fed, a tomb fit for the title, and nothing done by halves.\n\nThe steward's courier brought the colony a list of what the household cannot find in time, sealed with the family's crest.

[wedding,royalhost] {DEAD} of {FACTION} is to be married at {PLACE}, and a noble wedding of the Empire has to look as if it lacks nothing. The household is short of what it needs and would rather the region didn't find out.\n\nA courier in livery brought the colony the list and asked for an answer in writing.

li.label: Accept the terms
li.outcome: The rider went home with the colony's yes.

li.label: Decline
li.outcome: {FACTION} will take their list to the next village.

terms.li: The list: {ITEM}, all of it in the colony's stockpiles within {DAYS} of the colony agreeing (sculptures can stand anywhere on the map, as long as they aren't forbidden).\n\nFor everything, {FACTION} will pay {COUNT} silver, well over its worth. If at least half of each thing is ready, they'll take what there is at its plain worth. Less than that, and they'll go elsewhere and think less of the colony for it.

accepted.li: [funeral] {DEAD}'s funeral at {PLACE} will have the colony's goods: {ITEM}, ready within {DAYS}. {FACTION}'s carts will come to collect.
[wedding] The colony has promised {ITEM} for {DEAD}'s wedding at {PLACE}, ready within {DAYS}. {FACTION}'s carts will come to collect.

ready.li: Everything on {FACTION}'s list is in the stockpiles. Their carts are due within {DAYS}.
[funeral] The last of the goods for {DEAD}'s funeral is stacked and counted. {FACTION}'s carts are on the road, due within {DAYS}.
[wedding] Everything for {DEAD}'s wedding is stacked and ready, and someone has tied a ribbon round the pile. {FACTION}'s carts are due within {DAYS}.

reminder.li: {FACTION}'s carts come within {DAYS}, and the list still isn't filled: {ITEM}.
[funeral] {DEAD} will be buried in {DAYS}, and {FACTION} are still counting on the colony for {ITEM}.
[wedding] {DEAD}'s wedding is in {DAYS}. {FACTION} have sent to ask, politely, how the colony is getting on with {ITEM}.

done.li: [delivered,funeral] {FACTION}'s carts are coming for everything the colony set aside, and their driver will pay {ITEM} silver for it.\n\nWhen {DEAD} is buried, there will be food for every family of {PLACE} at the graveside.

[delivered,wedding] {FACTION}'s carts are coming for everything the colony set aside, with {ITEM} silver in payment. The guests from {PLACE} at {DEAD}'s wedding will know where the food on the tables came from.

[delivered,funeral,rite] {FACTION}'s carts are coming for everything the colony set aside, and their driver will pay {ITEM} silver for it. {DEAD} will be laid to rest with {RITE}, and the colony's food will feed the mourners afterwards.

[delivered,wedding,rite] {FACTION}'s carts are coming for everything the colony set aside, with {ITEM} silver in payment. {DEAD}'s wedding will be held with {RITE}, and the colony's goods will be on the tables.
[partial] Only part of {FACTION}'s list is ready. Their carts are coming for what there is and will pay its plain worth, {ITEM} silver. They will look for the rest at the next village.

fail.li: [missed,funeral] There wasn't nearly enough ready for {FACTION}'s carts to come for it. {DEAD} will be buried with what the town could find.\n\n{FACTION} had counted on the colony.

[missed,wedding] There wasn't nearly enough ready for {FACTION}'s carts to come for it. {DEAD}'s wedding will go ahead with plain bread and borrowed benches, and {FACTION} know the colony did not keep its promise.

cancelled.li: {FACTION} are no longer on terms with the colony, and the order for {PLACE} is off.
[funeral] {FACTION} have broken with the colony, and will bury {DEAD} without its help.
[wedding] {FACTION} have broken with the colony. {DEAD} will be married without anything of the colony's on the tables.

texts.li: [lowtech] "Have you seen {BEAST}?" asked the herder from {PLACE}, out of breath from running. {BEAST} is the town's prize {THING}. Three nights ago {BEAST} broke through a fence and ran off toward the colony's land, and none of {FACTION} can get a rope near {BEAST}.\n\nIf the colony can tame {BEAST} and hand {BEAST} back, {FACTION} will pay {COUNT} silver and be grateful besides. {A_nameDef} thinks it can be done.

[!lowtech] {FACTION}'s breeders at {PLACE} have lost {BEAST}, a prize {THING} with a pedigree going back six generations. {BEAST} jumped a fence three nights ago, has been running wild near the colony's land ever since, and won't let any of their people near.\n\nIf the colony can tame {BEAST} and hand {BEAST} back, {FACTION} will pay {COUNT} silver. {A_nameDef} thinks it can be done.

[skill:Animals] {FACTION}'s herder came up the road looking for {BEAST}, the prize {THING} of {PLACE}, which has a good coat and wears a braided halter. {BEAST} has been loose for three days near the colony's land, and the town's people can't get anywhere near.\n\nIf the colony can tame {BEAST} and hand {BEAST} back, {FACTION} will pay {COUNT} silver. {A_nameDef} knows animals and would like to try.

[winter] A herder from {PLACE} came through the snow looking for {BEAST}, the prize {THING} of {FACTION}. {BEAST} broke out in the last storm and ran off toward the colony's land, and it is getting colder.\n\nIf the colony can tame {BEAST} and hand {BEAST} back before the worst of it, {FACTION} will pay {COUNT} silver. {A_nameDef} thinks it can be done.

li.label: Accept the terms
li.outcome: The herder went home to wait for word.

li.label: Decline
li.outcome: The herder goes looking for help elsewhere.

terms.li: Tame {BEAST} within {DAYS} of the colony agreeing. {BEAST} will be loose somewhere on the colony's land: mark {BEAST} to be tamed, and send {A_nameDef} or another good handler.\n\nHanded back unharmed, {BEAST} is worth {COUNT} silver to {FACTION}. If {BEAST} gets away, they'll be disappointed; if {BEAST} is killed, they'll take it hard.

accepted.li: Somewhere on the colony's land, {BEAST} is running loose, and {FACTION} are waiting. Mark {BEAST} to be tamed within {DAYS}.
{A_nameDef} has promised {FACTION}'s herder to bring {BEAST} in. Mark {BEAST} to be tamed before {DAYS} are out.

reminder.li: {BEAST} is still wild, and will wander off for good unless tamed within {DAYS}.
{FACTION}'s herder has sent to ask after {BEAST} again. {DAYS} left to tame {BEAST}.

done.li: [returned] {FACTION}'s herder is coming to take {BEAST} home, with {ITEM} silver and the thanks of {PLACE}.
[bought] {FACTION} have taken the colony's silver, and {BEAST} belongs to the colony now.

fail.li: [killed] {BEAST}, the prize {THING} of {PLACE}, is dead on the colony's land. {FACTION} took the news hard; {BEAST} was worth more to them than silver.
[escaped] Nobody tamed {BEAST} in time, and {BEAST} is heading off into the hills. {FACTION} have sent word that they're disappointed.
[lost] {BEAST} is gone from the colony's land, and {FACTION} have no idea where. Their herder is out looking again, alone.
[kept] The colony tamed {BEAST} and kept {BEAST} without paying anything. {FACTION} are angry about it and will tell the other towns.

cancelled.li: {FACTION} have turned against the colony. Whatever becomes of {BEAST} now is the colony's own business.
Word came that {FACTION} want nothing more to do with the colony. {BEAST} is the colony's own problem now.

texts.li: {BEAST} has been tamed and follows the colony's handlers around as if {BEAST} had always lived here. {FACTION}'s herder has heard and is ready to come for {BEAST}.\n\nHand {BEAST} back, and the {TALE} silver promised is the colony's. Or the colony could keep {BEAST}: {FACTION} would sell {BEAST} for {COUNT} silver. Keeping {BEAST} without paying would make them angry.

[skill:Animals] {A_nameDef} has tamed {BEAST}, and {BEAST} now eats from {A_possessive} hand. {FACTION}'s herder has heard and is waiting to hear what the colony will do.\n\n{TALE} silver if {BEAST} goes home, as promised. {COUNT} silver, paid to {FACTION}, if the colony would rather keep {BEAST}. Or the colony could simply keep {BEAST} and pay nothing.

{BEAST} is tame at last and follows the colony's handlers around. The herder from {PLACE} has sent to ask when to come.\n\nThe herder will take {BEAST} home and pay the {TALE} silver promised. If the colony has grown fond of {BEAST}, {FACTION} would sell {BEAST} for {COUNT} silver. The herder also made it clear that they would not take it well if the colony kept {BEAST} for nothing.

li.label: Keep {BEAST}, and pay {COUNT} silver
li.outcome: {BEAST} stays with the colony, and the herder is paid for it.

li.label: Keep {BEAST} without paying
li.outcome: {BEAST} stays with the colony, and the herder is not paid for it.

titles.li: A place for the pilgrims to pray
A shrine on the pilgrims' road

texts.li: [lowtech] The elders of {PLACE} have sent a request. Every year the pilgrims of {FACTION} walk from {PLACE} to a holy spring in the far hills, and their road crosses the colony's land, where there is nowhere for them to stop and pray. They ask the colony to make them a shrine: a sculpture made by hand, standing under the open sky.\n\nIf a shrine is there, the pilgrims will pray at it, leave an offering and remember who made it. {A_nameDef} already has an idea for it.

[!lowtech] Pilgrims of {FACTION} walk from {PLACE} to an old monastery in the far hills every year, and the road they take crosses the colony's land. This year the elders of {PLACE} have written to ask whether the colony would put up a shrine along the way: a carving or a statue, out in the open, where the walkers can stop and pray.\n\nThe pilgrims would leave an offering, and remember who raised it. {A_nameDef} already has an idea for it.

[skill:Artistic] The elders of {PLACE} have sent a request that interests {A_nameDef}. Pilgrims of {FACTION} pass the colony every year on their way to the far hills, and the elders would like a shrine on the colony's land for them to pray at: something made by hand, under the open sky.\n\nIf it's there when the pilgrims come, they'll pray, leave an offering and remember who made it. {A_nameDef} has started sketching.

li.label: Accept the terms
li.outcome: The messenger went back to the elders with the colony's promise.

li.label: Decline
li.outcome: The pilgrims will pray by the roadside, as they always have.

terms.li: A sculpture of {TALE} quality or better, standing under the open sky (no roof over any part of it) on the colony's land, within {DAYS} of the colony agreeing. Once it stands, word goes out and the pilgrims set off; they arrive a day or so later.\n\nTheir offering will come to about {COUNT} silver, and {FACTION} will think well of the colony. If there's no shrine when they come, they'll walk on past, and their elders will hear of it.

accepted.li: The colony will raise a shrine for the pilgrims of {FACTION}: a sculpture of {TALE} quality or better, under the open sky, within {DAYS}.
{A_nameDef} has sent the colony's word to {PLACE}. A shrine for the pilgrims, a sculpture of {TALE} quality or better under the open sky, within {DAYS}.

ready.li: Word of the colony's shrine has reached {PLACE}. {ITEM} stands ready, and the pilgrims are on the road; they'll arrive in about {DAYS}.
A rider has gone to {PLACE} to tell the elders that {ITEM} stands waiting under the sky. The pilgrims should arrive in about {DAYS}.

reminder.li: The pilgrims of {FACTION} are coming within {DAYS}, and there's no shrine for them yet: a sculpture of {TALE} quality or better, under the open sky.
Still no shrine for the pilgrims of {FACTION}, and {DAYS} left to raise one: a sculpture of {TALE} quality or better, open to the sky.

done.li: [blessed] The pilgrims of {FACTION} are coming up the road to the colony's shrine, as their elders asked, and will spend the day beside it. They will leave an offering of {ITEM} silver at its foot and take word of the colony home to {PLACE}.

[blessed] The pilgrims of {FACTION} have reached the colony's land and are on their way to the shrine, to spend the day beside it. They bring an offering of {ITEM} silver to leave at its foot, and the elders of {PLACE} will hear about the shrine.

fail.li: [noshrine] There was no shrine for the pilgrims of {FACTION}, so they passed the colony by and prayed at the roadside as they always have. The elders of {PLACE} will hear of it.
[gone] The shrine the pilgrims of {FACTION} were coming to pray at was gone before they got here, so they passed the colony by. The elders of {PLACE} will hear of that too.

cancelled.li: With {FACTION} at odds with the colony, their pilgrims will take another road.
Word came that {FACTION} want nothing more to do with the colony. The pilgrims of {PLACE} will walk another road this year.
